svg.title: Status: libraries* 100.0%, hardware 100.0%

g.title: libc: 150 functions, ok
libmpeg: 103 functions, ok - Movies play at real speed with sound (native libmpeg2 decoder, native sound engine); audio trails picture ~0.1 s, constant
libkernel: 101 functions, ok - Runs natively; DelayThread on the scheduler, no timer register access
libmc2: 90 functions, ok - Native memory-card service; load and save verified (savetest)
C++ EH: 34 functions, ok
libgcc: 32 functions, ok
sif: 24 functions, ok - RPC as direct native calls
fileio: 15 functions, ok
libscf: 14 functions, ok
libm: 14 functions, ok
loadfile: 14 functions, ok
libpad2: 13 functions, ok - Native pad read on the EE (keyboard / gamepad)
libdbc: 11 functions, ok - dbcman RPC answered by native pad services
libcdvd: 10 functions, ok - CD reads served from the extracted game files (disc-usa/); the ISO only with GOW_ISO
libdma: 8 functions, ok - sceDmaSend feeds VIF/GIF directly; no DMA controller model
libgraph: 7 functions, ok - Display setup is a native override (GS display state, no GS register access)
libipu: 5 functions, ok - Served by the native decoder

libvib: 2 functions, ok - DualShock 2 actuators -> host gamepad rumble (Windows: XInput pads, DualShock 4 / DualSense over USB through HID, Bluetooth opt-in; raylib elsewhere); verified by the user on a real DualShock 4 over USB (2026-10-13)
R3000A CPU: no interpreter on the hot path (ok)
SPU2: native sound engine driven by LIBSD's exports (ok)
The game's 8 IRX modules compiled ahead of time to C++ (ok)
SIF: RPC and DMA as direct native calls (ok)
CDVD: the game's reads served from the extracted files (no drive model) (ok)
Pad: native service (SIO2 chip model deleted) (ok)
Memory card: native service, load/save verified (ok)
R5900 CPU: game code statically recompiled to C++ (6.4k functions) (ok)
Kernel: threads, semaphores, alarms, syscalls (native HLE) (ok)
FPU (COP1) and MMI instructions (ok)
INTC: not accessed by game code in gameplay (ok)
DMA controller: no model, packets go straight to VIF/GIF (ok)
Timers: native EE clock (game code calls it, counts computed from guest cycles); T2 users (DelayThread) on the scheduler (ok)
GS: native OpenGL render-target renderer, 2x internal, 16:9; display registers native (ok)
VIF1 decoded directly; VU1 microprograms compiled ahead of time to C++ (ok)
Textures and CLUT: native texture store; palettes from render targets read on the GPU (ok)
GIF (PATH1-3): the game's GIF tags fed to the renderer (ok)
IPU: replaced by the native MPEG-2 decoder (libmpeg2); movies play at real speed with sound (ok)

svg.text: * Functions of the static Sony libraries linked into SCUS_973.99 (recompiled output). Hardware: weighted per component.
